(א) (4) There. Exempt from Kriat Shema and tefillah. And immediately when they begin to throw earth upon the deceased he recites and prays. And so did Maharil. And it seems that before chatzos he prays Shacharis as written in siman 89. Magen Avraham end of note 1. Sha'ar HaTziyun note 2. Rabbenu Zalman note 1. And likewise in responsum Devar Moshe vol. 3 siman 13, and they brought it in Shulchan Aruch HaRav p. 282 side a. Sha'arei Teshuvah note 1. But the Zera Emes vol. 1 siman 11 disagreed with the words of the Magen Avraham mentioned, and he ruled practically that when the mourner returns from the house of graves after a third of the day he should not say even the prayer of the eighteen [blessings], only it is fitting that he recite Keri'as Shema alone without blessings to accept upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of heaven; and he wrote that such is the custom in the city of Modena, see there. And they brought it from Machberes note 1 in Shulchan Aruch HaRav there. Sha'arei Teshuvah there. Siddur Beit Yosef in the laws of Keri'as Shema of Maariv note 10. And likewise the Chesed LeAvraham note 1. And he need not complete the tefillah after it since at the time of his obligation he was exempt, as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 341 seif 2; and likewise Eliyah Rabbah note 1. Rabbenu Zalman there. Sha'arei Teshuvah there. Chesed LeAvraham there. And see in our words above siman 58 note 25.

(ב) (4) And he wrote there — the Magen Avraham: but Birchos HaShachar he should not say, since at the time of his obligation he was exempt, as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 341 seif 2 regarding Havdalah, so far. And they cited Eliyah Rabbah there, Sha'ar HaTziyun there. And likewise Rabbenu Zalman there — that he should not say all Birchos HaShachar even if he was buried before the time of Keri'as Shema and tefillah passed, since at the hour when the obligation of the blessings applied — that is, when he rose from his bed — he was exempt from them; he need not complete them afterwards, and if he blesses he blesses in vain, so far. And likewise ruled Devar Moshe in his responsum vol. 3 siman 13 per the view of the Magen Avraham mentioned; only to distinguish — the three blessings "who did not make me a gentile," "who did not make me a slave," and "who did not make me a woman," and the blessings of the Torah that are upon a person to say them all day — also the mourner after his relative was buried — at any time he is obligated to say them, see there. And they brought Shulchan Aruch HaRav there. And see Levush and Machatzis HaShekel what they wrote on the words of the Magen Avraham mentioned; and it is implied from their words that these words of the Magen Avraham apply specifically per those who say that these blessings — if one was not obligated in them — one does not bless them; but per those who say they were instituted for the conduct of the world and even if one was not obligated in them one blesses them, as written in siman 46 seif 8, one may bless them also after chatzos, see there. And likewise the Peri Megadim in Eshel Avraham note 1, and likewise the Nahar Shalom note 1, and likewise the Maamar Mordechai note 3 — only that he wrote the matter needs study, see there. And likewise Rabbi Meir Chaim z"l p. 244 sides b and c — that the mourner may bless them all day long; and he wrote that in his days they did so in practice with the consent of the gaon Maharit, author of Erech HaShulchan, see there. And see in Siddur Nehora HaShalem in Derech HaChaim in the laws of Pesukei DeZimra and Birchos HaShachar — he wrote in the name of Sefer Ma'aseh Rav from the gaon Maharal of Vilna z"l — that one who forgot and did not say Birchos HaShachar before tefillah may say them afterwards all day, and also at night until sleep, except the blessing of the Torah which already departed in Ahavah Rabbah and the blessing Elokei Neshamah which departed in the blessing Mechayeh HaMetim, see there. And so is implied from the words of the Maamar Mordechai siman 46 note 10 — only that he is uncertain in this; only he wrote it seems simple that until the end of three hours of the day one may bless with simplicity, for such is the way of princes to stand three hours and it is still the hour of rising, and many people do not rise until that hour — and if so there is no law and no judge who can bless; but for the rest of the day there is room to doubt, see there. And likewise in Siddur Nehora HaShalem in Derech HaChaim in the laws of onen note 4 — if the aninus continued until after four hours of Birchos HaShachar, that is, what is before Keri'as Shema, he should not say them even if he has leisure, since they said in the Gemara for all these blessings there is a time, as written — when he puts on his shoes he blesses, etc.; and even though we rule in siman 46 that for the needs of the world one blesses, and even if one was awake all night one blesses all the needs of the world — that is, until the time of rising which is a third of the day, like Keri'as Shema — see siman 58; except the blessing of the Torah and the blessing "who did not make me a gentile," "who did not make me a slave," and "who did not make me a woman" — those blessings one blesses all day, and even after chatzos if he was buried he says them, so far. And see the gaon Maharshak z"l in Sefer Shenos Chaim siman 80 p. 22 side d — he wrote that one who did not bless Birchos HaShachar until chatzos may not bless afterwards, see there; and his reason seems to me that they instituted them to be said until chatzos when the strength of the day still ascends, and not after chatzos when the shadows of evening begin to incline. And the Zera Emes there wrote that even after tefillah all day long he may say them, as written in siman 52, see there. It turns out that in the view of the plain speakers there are three disputes in the matter: some say the time of Birchos HaShachar is until a third of the day like the time of Keri'as Shema; and some say until chatzos like the time of the morning tefillah; and some say all day long is its time. However, what the Magen Avraham wrote and his colleagues regarding onen that he should not say them afterwards even if he was buried before the time of Keri'as Shema and tefillah passed — we do not rule like him, since we ruled above in siman 46 note 49 per the Ari z"l and the later authorities that for the conduct of the world they are said; and if so the matter is not dependent on him but on any time the world can say them — he too can say them if his dead was buried before that time. However, the words of the Ari z"l remain for us in Sha'ar HaKavanos p. 2 side b — he wrote the blessing "who gives strength to the weary" is one of these eighteen blessings instituted before tefillah, etc.; and on p. 1 side c he wrote these eighteen blessings are in Ze'ir Anpin of Asiyah; and likewise in Peri Etz Chaim sha'ar HaBerachot ch. 3, see there. And further see in Nahar Shalom p. 11 side c on the Noda BiYehudah in the matter "in general the first three blessings," etc.; and in our words to siman 46 note 18 in the matter "and this," see there — that it is implied they have no place after tefillah, since they were instituted for all aspects of the three lower worlds in Yetzirah and ascended to Atzilut and the mochin are drawn through tefillah — how can the repair come afterwards, as the elder asked the children. Therefore it seems for the practical law that if one delayed and has not yet prayed — since he can pray until chatzos of the day, he can also bless Birchos HaShachar, since the repair of tefillah has not yet been done through it he can bless Birchos HaShachar before tefillah; and the same for onen if his dead was buried before chatzos that he can pray afterwards — only per the reasoning of the Zera Emes and his colleagues who wrote he cannot pray except until a third of the day — he also should not bless Birchos HaShachar except until a third of the day. And all other people — if one forgot to bless them before tefillah and wants to bless them afterwards, if it is before a third of the day we do not neglect him, but not afterwards because there is a dispute in this as mentioned — requires investigation, and even though the Ari z"l wrote they were instituted for the conduct of the world and a person must bless them every day — requires investigation; we do not say "requires investigation" against the words of the Ari z"l — that is, specifically regarding whether he was awake all night or did not remove his turban, etc., but not regarding that he should bless them at any time, for their time is before tefillah as mentioned. However, the blessing of the Torah one may bless at any time of the day if he did not bless it, because it has two kavanos as written in siman 46 note 29; and further see in our words to siman 46 note 9.

(ג) (4) There. Exempt from Kriat Shema, etc. And the same — that he is exempt from all mitzvos mentioned in the Torah; and so it states explicitly in the Gemara. Olas Tamid note 3.

levushei_serad.he: <small>(מ"א סק"א)</small> הבדלה. אמת דשם פסק בש"ע דיבדיל אחר הקבורה עד יום ג' וא"כ מביא המג"א ראיה לסתור אך כוונת המג"א משום דהב"י מביא פלוגתא שם בזה דהרא"ש וסייעתו ס"ל דפטור מהבדלה כיון דבשעת חובתו היה פטור ומביא ראיה מחגיגה דחיגר בראשון של הרגל ונתפשט ביום ב' פטור מן הראיה אע"פ דראיה נוהגת כל שבעה מ"מ כולהו תשלומין דראשון נינהו וכיון שהיה פטור ביום א' פטור לגמרי ה"נ בהבדלה ושאר פוסקים חולקים וטעמא משום דהכא אין תשלומין כלל אלא דחיוב דהבדלה נמשך מן מוצאי שבת עד יום ג' ולא בתורת תשלומין כלל דמה"ט מתפלל עד חצות אע"פ דבבוקר היה פטור משום דאין בזה תשלומין אלא דזמן תפלה נמשך מהבוקר עד חצות ומש"ה פסק שם בש"ע דמבדיל וכהנך פוסקים וס"ל למג"א דברכת השחר דמי לההוא דחיגר כיון דאמרינן בש"ס כי שמע קול תרנגול' כו' וכן בכולהו רק שכתבו הפוסקים הובא בש"ע סי' מ"ו דעכשיו מפני שאין הידים נקיות וגם מפני ע"ה נהגו לסדרם בבה"כ א"כ מיקרי תשלומין כיון דהחיוב חל על מעשה כגון קריאת התרנגול ומדינ' מיד כי שמע צריך לברך כנלע"ד כוונת המג"א וק"ל:
levushei_serad.en: (Magen Avraham note 1) Havdalah. It is true that there he ruled in Shulchan Aruch that one makes Havdalah after the burial until the third day; and if so the Magen Avraham brings proof to the contrary — but the intention of the Magen Avraham is because the Beit Yosef brings a dispute there — that the Rosh and his supporters hold he is exempt from Havdalah since at the time of his obligation he was exempt; and he brings proof from Chagigah — one who was lame on the first day of the festival and was healed on the second day is exempt from the pilgrimage offering even though the pilgrimage offering applies all seven [days] — nevertheless all of them are compensations of the first day; and since he was exempt on day one he is entirely exempt. So too regarding Havdalah. And other poskim disagree, and the reason is because here there are no compensations at all, rather the obligation of Havdalah extends from Motzei Shabbos until the third day and not in the category of compensations at all — for why does one pray until chatzos even though in the morning he was exempt? Not because of compensations, but because the time of tefillah extends from morning until chatzos; and therefore he ruled there in Shulchan Aruch that one makes Havdalah. And these poskim hold, and the Magen Avraham holds, that Birchos HaShachar is comparable to the case of the lame one, since we say in Shas — when he heard the voice of the rooster, etc.; and so in all of them — only that the poskim wrote, brought in Shulchan Aruch siman 46, that nowadays because hands are not clean and also because of the evil eye they instituted to arrange them in the synagogue — if so it is called compensations since the obligation applies on an action such as hearing the rooster; and by law immediately when he hears he must bless, as seems to me the intention of the Magen Avraham — requires investigation.

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ד) תוך כו' לא הזכיר ד"א ר"ל דאפי' חוץ לד"א מן הקבר אסור וכ"כ ט"ז ולעיל סי' מ"ה נראה מדבריו דאפי' חוץ לקברות אם אין לו מחיצות אסור תוך ארבע אמות והיינו אם הוא תוך ארבע אמות של קבר וע"ש:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (note 4) Within, etc. — he did not mention four cubits; explanation: that even outside four cubits from the grave it is forbidden; and likewise the Taz. And above siman 45 it appears from his words that even outside cemeteries, if there are no partitions, it is forbidden within four cubits — and this is if he is within four cubits of a grave, see there.

peri_megadim.he: אבל עט״ז תיקן בזה קושיי׳ מ״א באות ג׳ דבמ״ש הואיל ויהיה פטור ראוי לקבל עמ״ש מבע״י אם אין מחשיך על התחום ועי״ד שמ״א מדיני שבת וי״ט ובא״ח תקמ״ח בזה:
peri_megadim.en: But — the Taz resolved here the difficulty of the Magen Avraham in note 3, in what he wrote "since he will be exempt, it is fit to accept" — see Magen Avraham from the outset if he does not make it dark regarding the boundary; and see Yoreh De'ah 341 regarding the laws of Shabbat and Yom Tov; and in Orach Chayyim 348 on this.

rabbi_akiva_eiger.en: <small>Magen Avraham, note 3</small> That the fifth wrote. It should read: that he wrote.

mechaber.he: החופר קבר למת פטור:
mechaber.en: One who digs a grave for the deceased is exempt.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ה] המשמר את המת וכו'. אפילו בספינה דחיישינן לעכברים, (ש"ס):
eliyah_rabbah.en: [5] One who guards the deceased, etc. Even on a ship, for we are concerned about mice (Shas).

kaf_hachayim.he: ה) שם פטור מק"ש ומתפלה, מקום שנוהגים שכתפים מיוחדים להוציא המת ולאחר שנתעסקו הקרובים בצורכי הקבורה ימסרוהו להם והם יקברוהו משמסרוהו להם מותרים הקרובים בבשר ויין אפי' קודם שהוציאוהו מהבית ששוב אינו מוטל עליהם, יו"ד סי' שמ"א סעי' ג', וכתב שם הברכ"י אות ך' דה"ה דיכול לברך ולהתפלל כי היכי דשרי בירושלמי בבשר ויין פ' ואלו מגלחין בהוראת ר"י על מי שמת בתפיסה דמשלמסר לכתפין פסקה אנינות וכן מוכח מדברי המ"מ ריש פ' מי שמתו והכי משמע מתלמודין התם וכ"כ הרב מהריק"ש בהגהותיו דלשאר דיני אבילות נמי דינו כבשר ויין עכ"ל, וכ"כ מהר"י עייאש שם בס' שבט יהודה יעו"ש, והביאו ש"ץ דקפ"א ע"ד ושע"ת בזה הסי' אות א'. וכ"כ המש"ז אות ה' וז"ל ויראה דה"ה שמותר להתפלל ולקרות ק"ש בלא תפלין עכ"ד:
kaf_hachayim.en: (5) There. Exempt from Kriat Shema and tefillah. In a place where they practice that special bearers take out the deceased, and after the relatives were occupied with the needs of the burial they hand him over to them and they bury him — from when they hand him over to them the relatives are permitted in meat and wine even before they removed him from the house, since he is no longer imposed upon them, Yoreh De'ah siman 341 seif 3. And he wrote there the Birkei Yosef note 20 — that the same applies, that one may bless and pray, for just as it is permitted in the Yerushalmi in meat and wine in the chapter Ve'Eilu Megalchin in the ruling of Rabbenu Yerucham on one who died in captivity — that when they hand over to the bearers the aninus ceases; and so is proven from the words of the Maggid Mishneh at the beginning of the chapter Mi SheMeto; and so is implied from the Talmudim there; and likewise the rabbi Maharikash in his glosses — that for the other laws of mourning too his law is like meat and wine, so far. And likewise Mahari Ayash there in Sefer Shevet Yehudah, see there. And they brought Shulchan Aruch HaRav p. 281 side d and Sha'arei Teshuvah in this siman note 1. And likewise the Mishbetzos Zahav note 5, and these are his words: and it appears that the same applies — that it is permitted to pray and recite Kriat Shema without tefillin, so far.

levushei_serad.he: <small>(סק"ג)</small> דהא כתב הרב"י. ר"ל דאמ"ש הטור דחייב גם לעת ערב פי' הרב"י דכוונתו בשאר מצות דאי בק"ש ממ"נ כו' וא"כ אין מקום לדברי הב"ח:
levushei_serad.en: (note 3) For he wrote the Rabbeynu Yosef. Explanation: that when the Tur wrote he is obligated also at evening time — the Rabbeynu Yosef explained his intention is regarding other mitzvos; but if regarding Kriat Shema, in any case, etc.; and if so there is no place for the words of the Bach.

mishnah_berurah.he: (יג) פטור - אפילו בשעת נוחו מעט שגם אז נקרא עדיין עוסק במצוה שעי"ז יתחזק כוחו לחזור ולחפור:
mishnah_berurah.en: (13) He is exempt — even at his time of slight rest, for even then he is still called engaged in the mitzvah, for thereby his strength will be strengthened to return and dig.

peri_megadim.he:
או עט״ז וזה דלא כנראה מדברי המ״א אות ד׳:
אם אונן שבירך ושמעו אחרים אי יוצאין י״ח או נימא כל שאין מחויב בדבר מיקרי כיון דלעת עתה פטור הוא כתבנו בפתיחה כוללת מזה. ומיהו העוסק בצ״צ ופסק וקרא ושמעו אחרים שפיר יי״ח דלאו פטור ממש אלא שעוסק במצוה אחרת. ועי״ד שמ״א בט״ז ה׳ ועמ״א צ״ג אות ה׳ ואי״ה שם יבואר:
עי״ד שמ״א ס״ג דאעפ״י שיש מי שיתעסק בצרכי קבורה אסור בבשר ויין ופטור מכל המצות אבל אם מסרו לכתפיים מיוחדים לכך מותר בבשר ויין ויראה ה״ה שמותר להתפלל ולקרות ק״ש בלא תפילין: בסימן ל״ח כתבנו בחה״מ מניח תפילין אבל ביום א׳ ועא״ר שם ואיכא לעיוני בה דמ״מ יום מר הוא לו ומכ״ש דעת המחבר בסי׳ ל״א דבלא״ה חה״מ אין להניח תפילין ואף שאין אבילות במועד אנינות נוהג בחה״מ ואפי׳ בי״ט שני ע״י ישראל או בי״ט ראשון ע״י עממין ואי״ה בתקמ״ח יבואר עוד בזה:
peri_megadim.en:
Or — the Taz; and this does not appear [to agree] with the words of the Magen Avraham, note 4.

If — an onen who blessed and others heard him, do they fulfill [their obligation]? Or shall we say: anything one is not obligated in is called [exempt], since for the present he is exempt — we wrote this in a comprehensive introduction from this. However, one engaged in guarding the deceased who stopped and read and others heard — they fulfill well, for he is not truly exempt but engaged in another mitzvah. And see Yoreh De'ah 341 in the Taz, note 5, and Magen Avraham 393, letter 5; and there it will be explained.

See Yoreh De'ah 341 — even though there is someone who will attend to burial needs, meat and wine are forbidden and he is exempt from all mitzvot; but if they handed him over to bearers designated for this, meat and wine are permitted; and it appears that likewise he is permitted to pray and read Shema without tefillin. In siman 38 we wrote that on Chol HaMoed he dons tefillin, but on the first day; and in Ohr Chadash there; and there is room to examine it, for nevertheless it is a bitter day for him; and all the more so the view of the author in siman 31, that in any case on Chol HaMoed one does not don tefillin; and even though there is no mourning on the festival, onenut applies on Chol HaMoed, even on the second day of Yom Tov through Israel or the first day of Yom Tov through gentiles; and there, in 348, this will be explained further.

rabbi_akiva_eiger.he: <small>שם בא"ד </small>ומ"מ במ"ש הכל קורין אין זה על כל האבלים רק רצה בזה לאלם קושייתו על הב"ח לפי המנהג דכל העולם קבלו לחיוב לקרות ק"ש ולהתפלל במ"ש אחר צה"כ ואז האבל כבר חל עליו אנינות וע' בט"ז ודו"ק. נ"ה:
rabbi_akiva_eiger.en: <small>There, in Chacham Adam</small> And nevertheless, in what he wrote "all read" — this is not on all the mourners; he only wished thereby to silence his difficulty on the Bach, per the custom that the whole world accepted as obligation to read Shema and pray in what he wrote after tzeit hakochavim; and then mourning had already applied to him as onenut — see the Taz, and examine. So it appears to me.

mechaber.he: היו ב' או יות' חופרים כל הצריכים לצרכי החפיר' בבת אחת פטורים ואם יש נוספים נשמטים וקורין וחוזרין אלו ומתעסקים והאחרים נשמטים וקורין (עיין ביו"ד סימן שס"ה):
mechaber.en: If there were two or more diggers — all who are needed for the needs of the digging at one time are exempt; and if there are additional ones they slip away, recite, and return and occupy themselves, and the others slip away and recite [see Yoreh De'ah siman 365]. (.

beur_hagra.he: ס"ו כל הצריכין כו'. דוקא בכוך שאינו מחזיק אלא א' אמרו היו שנים כו' תה"א:
beur_hagra.en: Seif 66, all who need, etc. Specifically in a coffin that holds only one — they said there were two, etc. Toras HaAdam.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ו] אפילו אינו מתו וכו'. כלומר דאילו מתו אפילו אינו משמרו פטור, כיון שמוטל עליו לקברו כדלעיל:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [6] Even if it is not his deceased, etc. Meaning that if it were his deceased, even if he does not guard him he is exempt, since it is incumbent upon him to bury him as above.

kaf_hachayim.he: ו) שם ואפי' אם רוצה להחמיר וכו' אינו רשאי, מי שהתחיל להתפלל או לברך ברהמ"ז ונעשה אונן אם צריך שיפסיק או יגמור תפלתו או ברכתו עיין ברכ"י אות א' שהאריך בזה והביא מחלוקת הפוסקים דיש אומרים צריך להפסיק וי"א דא"צ להפסיק ולבסוף הניח הדבר לצדדין ולא הכריע יעו"ש. וגם הש"ץ דקע"ז ע"ג שקיל וטרי בהאי עניינא והביא דברי הברכ"י הנז' ולא הכריע כיעו"ש. מיהו הרב סידור בי"ע בדיני אנינות אות ח' הכריע כדעת מהרד"פ ז"ל דיפסיק יעו"ש, ואני אומר דמי שהוא רוצה שלא להפסיק אין מזניחין אותו כיון שיש לו על מה לסמוך רק שיכוין לבו לשמים ולישב דעתו לכוין בתפלתו או ברכתו. אח"כ ראיתי שכן פסק החס"ל אות ו':
kaf_hachayim.en: (6) There. And even if he wants to be strict, etc., he is not permitted — one who began to pray or to bless Birkas HaMazon and became an onen: whether he must stop or complete his tefillah or his blessing — see Birkei Yosef note 1 who expanded on this and brought the dispute of the poskim — some say he must stop and some say he need not stop; and in the end he left the matter undecided and did not decide, see there. And also Shulchan Aruch HaRav p. 277 side c weighed this matter and brought the words of the Birkei Yosef mentioned and did not decide, see there. However, the rabbi in Siddur Beit Yosef in the laws of aninus note 8 decided per the view of Maharadaf z"l that he stops, see there. And I say that one who wants not to stop — we do not neglect him since he has upon what to rely, only he should direct his heart to heaven and settle his mind to have kavanah in his tefillah or his blessing. Afterwards I saw that so ruled the Chesed LeAvraham note 6.

levushei_serad.he: <small>(שם)</small> במ"ש הכל קורין. והט"ז סק"ד כ' נ"ל כיון שיש עליו חיוב כו' מתרץ קושי' זו ומיושב קושי' הב"י וכוונת הטור גם על ק"ש:
levushei_serad.en: (there) In what is written "everyone recites." And the Taz note 4 wrote: it seems to me, since there is an obligation upon him, etc. — he resolves this difficulty and settles the difficulty of the Beit Yosef; and the intention of the Tur is also on Kriat Shema.

mishnah_berurah.he: (יד) והאחרים וכו' - ר"ל ונמצא שקראו כולם ולא נתבטל שום דבר מעסק הקבר כלל אפילו רגע:
mishnah_berurah.en: (14) And the others, etc. — meaning, and it turns out that all of them read, and nothing was canceled from the business of burial at all, even for a moment.

shaarei_teshuvah.he: ערב. עבה"ט ועיין ש"י סי' ח' דמ"ש ואף אם נימא דקאי גם על קריאת שמע לאו על הב"י קאי רק על הש"ע ע"ש. ועיין ביד אלי' סי' ט"ז דאם סמוך לשבת ואין זמן לקוברו חייב במנחה דע"ש שהרי הטעם כדי שיתעסק והא לא אפשר ע"ש. וכתכ בשירי כנה"ג יו"ד סי' שמ"א בש"ץ שמת לו מת בשבת והוא אונן לא גרע מאבל בחול כו' ה"נ אונן בשבת אם אין שם מי שיתפלל יכול האבל להתפלל ולהוצי' הרבים ידי חובתם. ואם יש שם אחר אינו יכול ע"ש ואנן נהגינן באבל בחול מתפלל אפי' בדאיכ' אחר והיינו כשמצוו' להתפלל על אביו ואמו. ולכן באונן בשבת לא יתפלל בדאיכא אחר. ועיין לקמן סי' קל"ג לענין קדיש קטן אונן בשבת ובמ"ש משבות יעקב בנעשה אונן פתאום. ועיין בש"צ בשם מוצל מאש ח"ב ומכתם לדוד שיש שדעתם שלא יסיים רק אותה ברכה אבל אין להתחיל ברכה אחרת. ובבר"י כאן האריך בזה וכתב בש"ץ שנראה שגם הוא דעתו שצריך להפסיק אלא שלא החליט ובש"ץ כתב השבט יהודה דעתו שצריך להפסיק ומשמע לי ג"כ שכן דעת המ"מ משום דאם יגמור איכא חשש ברכה לבטלה שב וא"ת עדיף ע"ש. ועיין בשבות יעקב ח"ב סי' קפ"ח לענין מת בר"ח אין מתפלל מוסף אם כבר עבר ז' שעות על היום ובבר"י ביו"ד סי' שמ"א חולק עליו ע"ש ויתבאר בהל' תפלה:
shaarei_teshuvah.en: Evening — in Avnei Nezer; and see Shiyurei Berachah, siman 8, in what he wrote; and even if we say it refers also to Keriyas Shema, it does not refer to the Beit Yosef but only to the Shulchan Aruch — see there. And see Yad Eliyahu, siman 16 — if it is near Shabbat and there is no time to bury him, he is obligated in Minchah with intent, for the reason is so that he should attend to it, and here it is not possible — see there. And so wrote in Shirrei Kenesses HaGedolah, Yoreh De'ah, siman 341, in Shabbos Shel Pesach — if his deceased died on Shabbat and he is an onen, he is not less than a mourner on a weekday, etc. So too an onen on Shabbat — if there is no one there to pray, the mourner may pray and discharge the obligation of the many. And if there is another there, he cannot — see there. And we practice that a mourner on a weekday prays even when another is present; and this is when they are commanded to pray for his father and mother. Therefore an onen on Shabbat does not pray when another is present. And see below, siman 133, regarding Kaddish; a minor onen on Shabbat; and in what he wrote from Shevut Yaakov regarding one who suddenly became an onen. And see in Shabbos Shel Pesach in the name of Motzal Me'esh, volume 2, and in a letter to David — there are those whose view is that he should not finish only that blessing, but he should not begin another blessing. And in Be'er Heitev here he elaborated on this and wrote in Shabbos Shel Pesach that it appears this is also his view, that he must stop, only he did not decide; and in Shabbos Shel Pesach wrote Shevet Yehudah that his view is he must stop; and it seems to me likewise that this is the view of the Maggid Mishneh, because if he finishes there is concern of a blessing in vain — return; and if you ask, stopping is preferable — see there. And see in Shevut Yaakov, volume 2, siman 188, regarding one who died on Rosh Chodesh — he does not pray Musaf if seven hours of the day have already passed; and in Be'er Heitev in Yoreh De'ah, siman 341, he disputes him — see there; and it will be explained in the laws of prayer.

mechaber.he: אסו' לקרות ק"ש תוך ד' אמות של מת או בבית הקברות ואם קרא לא יצא:
mechaber.en: It is forbidden to recite Keri'as Shema within four cubits of the deceased or in a cemetery; and if one recited, one did not fulfill one's obligation.

baer_heitev.he:
הקברות. ע"ל סי' מ"ה ס"ק א' מש"ש. ועיין מ"א סי' זה ס"ק ד':
לא יצא. אפילו היה שוגג כ"מ. והראב"ד חולק וס"ל דאין לחזור ולקרות. ופסק ע"ת לענין ברכות של קריאת שמע נקטינן כדברי המיקל דקי"ל ספק ברכות להקל. וכך פסק פר"ח דלק"ש יש לחוש לדברי הרמב"ם אבל אם בירך או התפלל אינו חוזר להתפלל ולברך דעיקר כדברי הראב"ד ע"ש. עיין ט"ז סי' זה ס"ק ה' ולעיל סי' מ"ה ס"ק א' ודו"ק:
baer_heitev.en:
The burials. See above siman 45 seif kaf alef from Shulchan Shelah. And see Magen Avraham on this siman seif daled.

He did not fulfill his obligation. Even if he was inadvertent, etc. And the Ra'avad disagrees and holds there is no returning to recite. And they ruled there regarding the blessings of Kriat Shema we hold like the lenient view, for we rule doubt regarding blessings leniently. And thus ruled Peri Chadash that for Kriat Shema one must be concerned for the Rambam's words, but if he blessed or prayed he does not return to pray and bless, for the essence follows the Ra'avad there. See Taz on this siman seif hei and above siman 45 seif alef, and understand carefully.

beer_hagolah.he:
ברכות י"ח וסוטה מ"ב
רמב"ם בפ"ג מהל' ק"ש:
beer_hagolah.en:
Berachos 18 and Sotah 42

Rambam in chapter 3 of Hilchos Kriat Shema

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ז] פטור. מיהו ודאי שכל שאינו צריך לטרוח כלל יצא ידי שניהם, מהיות טוב אל תקרא רע (בית יוסף):
eliyah_rabbah.en: [7] Exempt. However, it is certain that whoever does not need to exert himself at all fulfills both of them — from what is good do not call it bad (Beit Yosef).

kaf_hachayim.he: ז) שם ואם יש לו מי שישתדל בשבילו וכו' אין מוחין בידו, וכן סתם מרן ז"ל ביו"ד סי שמ"א סעי' א' דמדכתב שם וי"א דאינו רשאי משמע דלסתם מרן רשאי שאין מוחין בידו יעו"ש וכן פי' העו"ת והא"ר והברכ"י או' ב' דברי מרן ז"ל וכתבו הא"ר והברכ"י ז"ל דבזה אין מקום למה שהקשה על מרן ז"ל הל"ח ריש פ' מי שמתו יעו"ש וכ"כ עבה"ג סי' ס"ב יעו"ש. וא"כ לפי הכלל המסור בידינו דכל מקום שסותם מרן ז"ל ואח"כ כותב י"א דדעתו לפסוק כסתם כמש"ל סי' י"ג או' ז' א"כ הכא נמי דעתו לפסוק כמ"ש כאן דאם רוצה להחמיר אין מוחין בידו אם יש לו מי שישתדל בשבילו, וכ"כ א"ר באות הנז' וע"כ כיון שאנו קבלנו עלינו סברת מרן ז"ל ומרן הכי ס"ל אין למחות ביד מי שרוצה להחמיר וכן פסק סידור בי"ע בדיני ק"ש דערבית או' ח' ובדיני אנינות אות א'. ועוד עיין מש"ל סי' ה"ן אות י"ג:
kaf_hachayim.en: (7) There. And if he has someone who will exert himself on his behalf, etc. — they do not protest against him; and so Maran z"l ruled without qualification in Yoreh De'ah siman 341 seif 1 — for from what is written there "and some say he is not permitted," it is implied that per Maran's unqualified ruling he is permitted and they do not protest against him, see there. And so explained Olas Tamid and Eliyah Rabbah and Birkei Yosef note 2 on the words of Maran z"l; and Eliyah Rabbah and Birkei Yosef z"l wrote that in this there is no place for what the Lechem Chamudot challenged on Maran z"l at the beginning of the chapter Mi SheMeto, see there. And likewise Avodas HaGershuni siman 62, see there. And if so, per the rule transmitted to us that wherever Maran z"l rules without qualification and afterwards writes "and some say," his intention is to rule like the unqualified ruling as written in siman 13 note 7 — here too his intention is to rule as written here, that if he wants to be strict they do not protest against him if he has someone who will exert himself on his behalf; and likewise Eliyah Rabbah in the note mentioned. And therefore, since we accepted upon ourselves the reasoning of Maran z"l and Maran so held — one should not protest against one who wants to be strict; and so ruled Siddur Beit Yosef in the laws of Kriat Shema of Maariv note 8 and in the laws of aninus note 1. And further see what we wrote in siman 55 note 13.

magen_avraham.he:
תוך ד"א כו'. עמ"ש סי' מ"ה דלא כע"ת וכ"מ ברמזים פ"ג דגבי קברות לא הזכיר ד"א:
לא יצא. דקנסוהו חכמים הואיל ועבר על דבריהם אפילו היה שוגג [כ"מ]:
magen_avraham.en:
Within four cubits, etc. See siman 45, not like Eliyah Rabba; and so is implied in the hints ch. 83 that regarding cemeteries he did not mention four cubits.

He did not fulfill [his obligation]. For the Sages penalized him since he transgressed their words, even if he was inadvertent [so is implied].

mishnah_berurah.he:
(טו) ק"ש - וה"ה לומר קדיש ושאר דברי קדושה והטעם משום לועג לרש:
(טז) או בבה"ק - עיין לעיל בסי' מ"ה סק"א במ"ב מה שכתבתי שם לענין לכנוס בתוכו בתפילין וה"ה לענין זה:
(יז) לא יצא - קנסוהו חכמים הואיל ועבר על דבריהם אפילו היה שוגג והראב"ד חולק וס"ל דא"צ לחזור ולקרות כיון דהמקום ההוא היה ראוי לקרות בו ורק משום לועג לרש יצא בדיעבד ולדינא לענין ק"ש הסכימו האחרונים לחוש לדברי הרמב"ם לחזור ולקרות אבל אם בירך או התפלל אינו חוזר. ולענין ברכות ק"ש מסתפק הפמ"ג עי"ש טעמו:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(15) Shema — and the same applies to saying Kaddish and other holy matters; and the reason is because of scoffing of the wicked.

(16) Or in a synagogue — see above in siman 45, note 1 in Mishna Berurah what I wrote there regarding entering it with tefillin; and the same applies to this matter.

(17) He has not fulfilled his obligation — the Sages penalized him since he transgressed their words, even if it was unwitting; and the Ra'avad disagrees and holds that he need not return and read, since that place was fit to read in, and only because of scoffing of the wicked he fulfilled his obligation after the fact. And for practical law regarding Shema, the later authorities agreed to heed the words of the Rambam to return and read; but if he blessed or prayed, he does not return. And regarding the blessings of Shema the Peri Megadim is uncertain — see there his reason.

turei_zahav.he: או בב"הק. פי' או בתוך ד"א של קבר וע"כ אפילו דיעבד לא יצא אבל בב"הק חוץ לד"א של קבר אע"פ שאסור לכתחלה כמ"ש בסי' מ"ה לדעת הטור מכל מקום בדיעבד ודאי יצא ובטור חסר כאן או וכצ"ל או בתוך ד"א של מת:
turei_zahav.en: Or in a synagogue — meaning, or within four cubits of a grave; and therefore even after the fact he has not fulfilled his obligation. But in a synagogue outside four cubits of a grave — even though it is forbidden ab initio, as written in siman 45 per the Tur — nevertheless after the fact he certainly fulfills his obligation. And in the Tur the word "or" is missing here; and so it should read: or within four cubits of a deceased.
